summary: Enhance your skills in water resource management with our GIS training course. Learn to analyze and manage water resources effectively for sustainable solutions
lede: GIS for water resource management provides a structured way to capture, store, visualize, and analyze spatial information about water quality and quantity. This course connects hydrology with practical workflows for delineating watersheds, assessing land use and topography, modeling flood scenarios, and monitoring irrigation efficiency. Across five intensive days, you will work with digital elevation models, multi-criteria decision analysis, automated runoff estimation, and IoT sensor data in centralized geographic information systems. You will also apply SWAT and HEC-RAS for surface water modeling, calculate the SCS curve number, map groundwater vulnerability with DRASTIC, and use Sentinel-2 and Landsat imagery to support operational analysis when data and infrastructure are limited.
audienceIntro: This program is specifically designed for professionals who manage the intersection of spatial data and hydrological systems in government, consultancy, or utility sectors.
modules: Spatial Data Foundations for Water Management
Surface Water and Flood Risk Modeling
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of hydrological concepts and prior experience with general GIS software (ArcGIS or QGIS). Familiarity with spreadsheet data management is required. No programming or coding knowledge is necessary for this course.
